haiku-low.q1: It still signs in. Google sign-in matches by sub, not email, and Google sign-in never changes users.email.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter that account's password on the confirm form. A correct password links the sub and then the session starts.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5 the account locks for 15 minutes and the pending record is deleted, so nothing is linked.
haiku-low.q4: Verified email with no match: a new user is created with no password, linked to the sub, in one transaction, then a session starts. Unverified: refused, nothing created.
haiku-low.q5: The state record has expired or was already deleted by GETDEL, so the callback shows an error page. Nothing changes.
haiku-low.q6: A new 14-day sliding session row via start_session. Any existing sid session row is deleted, and a new sid cookie is set.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required, only a signed-in session with CSRF. If the sub is linked to another user, linking is refused and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis record oidc:tx:state, TTL 600 s, with the state value also in the oidc_tx cookie. GETDEL at the first callback deletes the record, the cookie is cleared, and TTL expires it.
haiku-low.q9: Redis record oidc:pending:id holds sub and user_id, TTL 600 s. The browser refers to it with the oidc_pending cookie. Deleted on success, on lock, or by TTL.
haiku-low.q10: In the PostgreSQL table google_identities. sub is the primary key, giving one user per Google account. user_id is UNIQUE, giving one Google account per user.
haiku-low.q11: The user sees an error page saying sign-in failed, try again. Nothing is written. The state is spent, and the exchange is not retried.
haiku-low.q12: The Redis record stores intent, login or link. A link also stores user_id, and the callback requires the signed-in user to match it or shows an error page.

sonnet.q1: Nothing breaks. Matching is by permanent `sub`, never email. The sub is found in google_identities, so if the linked user is not locked, start_session runs for that user. users.email is never changed by Google sign-in.
sonnet.q2: The user must confirm the password. The server stores a pending record in Redis (`oidc:pending:id`, TTL 600 s) and sets the `oidc_pending` cookie. It shows a password form that posts to /auth/google/confirm with CSRF protection. Only a correct password inserts the google_identities row and deletes the pending record in one transaction. Then start_session runs. This applies only if the user has no Google account yet and email_verified is true.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins, the same counter as password login. The pending record stays until its TTL, so the user can retry. At 5 failures locked_until is set to now plus 15 minutes and failed_logins resets to 0. That lock deletes the pending record and the oidc_pending cookie is cleared. The user sees Account temporarily locked and nothing is linked.
sonnet.q4: If email_verified is true and no user has that lowercased email: in one DB transaction it creates a user with NULL password_hash and email_verified_at = now, and inserts the google_identities row. Then start_session runs. If email_verified is false: refuse with a message to use email and password, and nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: Both cases fail. The Redis key has a 600 s TTL, so after 12 minutes the state is expired. A replayed callback finds nothing, because GETDEL already deleted the record. The user sees an error page and nothing changes. The user must start again.
sonnet.q6: The same kind of session as password login, created by start_session(user_id). If the browser sent a sid cookie, start_session first deletes that old session row. It then inserts a new row lasting 14 days and sliding forward, and sets the sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax). It redirects to return_to, or /home if return_to is invalid.
sonnet.q7: No password and no email match is required. The email addresses need not match, and linking uses only sub. The link must be started from a signed-in session with a CSRF token. If the sub is already linked to another user, the link is refused with a message on Settings that it is linked to someone else, and nothing changes.
sonnet.q8: In one Redis record, `oidc:tx:<state>`, with a 600 s TTL. It also holds intent, user_id (for link) and return_to. The browser holds the state value in the `oidc_tx` cookie (max age 600 s). The record is removed by GETDEL at the first callback, or by the TTL. The cookie is cleared at the callback.
sonnet.q9: It is held in the Redis record `oidc:pending:id` (TTL 600 s from the callback), which holds the sub and the matched user_id. The browser refers to it through the `oidc_pending` cookie, which has the same lifetime. The record is deleted on success, on lock, or by TTL. The cookie is cleared when the record is deleted.
sonnet.q10: In the new PostgreSQL table google_identities (sub, user_id, linked_at). The PRIMARY KEY on sub gives one user per Google account. The UNIQUE constraint on user_id gives one Google account per user. user_id also has a foreign key to users with ON DELETE CASCADE.
sonnet.q11: The user sees an error page saying sign-in failed, try again. Nothing is written. The state is already spent. The document does not describe any retry of the exchange. The user must start again from login or settings.
sonnet.q12: The intent field (login or link) stored in the Redis oidc:tx record. For a link, the record also stores the signed-in user_id. At the callback the server checks that the signed-in user equals the stored user_id. If they differ it shows an error page and nothing changes.
